summary: QuickCredit should be a hybrid, with one extra managed path beside the main service in ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Client: Next.js (web) + Compose Multiplatform (Android and iOS). Server: Spring Boot. Data: PostgreSQL (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL in ap-south-1 (Mumbai), Multi-AZ). Host: Amazon ECS on Fargate in ap-south-1 (Mumbai).

frontend.justification: QuickCredit is a fintech on android, ios, web. Twelve month target 300,000 users, peak 10,000, MVP 16 weeks, 8 senior engineers. React framework with server rendering and static export, so public pages can rank and logged-in screens can still be rich. Shared Kotlin UI for Android and iOS from JetBrains. It stays close to the Android SDK. Team languages: java, kotlin, typescript.

alternatives.why_not: React (Vite) (web) + Compose Multiplatform (Android and iOS) is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
Angular (web) + Compose Multiplatform (Android and iOS) is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.

tradeoffs: Heavier than a pure static generator when every page is Markdown.
Framework upgrades need attention each major.
iOS polish and the odd platform API still need device time.

backend.justification: The usual JVM server for a ledger, audit log, and long-lived transactions. Peak 10,000, workload balanced, realtime off. Money movement wants a boring server with transactions, not a function that forgets its connection pool.

alternatives.why_not: NestJS is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
Fastify is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.

tradeoffs: Slow cold start, so it is a poor Lambda citizen.
More boilerplate than FastAPI on a two-week build.

database.choice: PostgreSQL (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL in ap-south-1 (Mumbai), Multi-AZ)
database.justification: Relational, ACID, and available as a managed service in Mumbai, the EU, and the US. The default for money, bookings, and tenancy. Placement follows the host pin: ap-south-1 (Mumbai). availability 99.95 is why the database line is redundant, not a single node. A double-entry ledger needs commits that either land or do not. That is this engine, not a document store.

alternatives.why_not: Microsoft SQL Server is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
MySQL is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.

tradeoffs: A single small node will not meet 99.99 on its own. You pay for a standby.
Very large analytical scans want a column store beside it, not instead of it, once you pass a few terabytes.

hosting.choice: Amazon ECS on Fargate in ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
hosting.justification: cloud_preference is aws, deployment_model is managed_cloud, data_residency resolves to india. The pin is ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Containers in the region you pick, including ap-south-1 Mumbai, without running Kubernetes.

alternatives.why_not: Lambda cold starts and the 15 minute cap fight a long-lived server, sockets, or a ledger.
deployment_model is managed_cloud, so the team should not own the OS.

tradeoffs: IAM, VPC, and the load balancer are real work. A team with no operator will feel it.

supporting.justification: Peak concurrency is 10,000. A small cache holds sessions, OTP attempts, and hot reads so the database is not the first thing to fall over.

alternatives.why_not: The managed cache is the same protocol with backups and a patch cycle already solved.

tradeoffs: Another process to watch. At a small size it can share a node with the queue.

supporting.justification: Webhook and payout work should leave the request path. Payments, scoring, or write spikes should retry on their own.

alternatives.why_not: It adds a second system before the volume requires one.

tradeoffs: Poison messages need a dead-letter view, or they vanish into retries.

supporting.justification: Phone OTP for users in India should use a domestic SMS route (DLT-registered). MSG91 is that route. Store only a hash of the code, in the India database.

alternatives.why_not: It works, and it is a worse fit for the residency of the phone numbers.
The user record would sit in a Google project whose region story is easy to get wrong, and phone-auth pricing surprises small budgets.

tradeoffs: SMS cost scales with logins, not with servers. A noisy retry loop will blow the budget before the database does.

supporting.choice: Amazon S3 in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) with SSE-KMS
supporting.justification: Uploads have to live somewhere durable. The bucket is private. The app issues short-lived URLs. KYC, health, or customer files do not sit on a public CDN.

alternatives.why_not: A second file system splits retention and access reviews. One bucket next to the app is enough.

tradeoffs: Lifecycle rules are part of the design. Nobody deletes old uploads unless you ask the bucket to.

supporting.justification: Cache the public web bundle close to users. Private uploads and payment payloads go straight to the origin in the pinned region.

alternatives.choice: Cloudflare in front of the whole origin
alternatives.why_not: A global cache in front of personal data fights the residency pin.

tradeoffs: A bad cache key will serve one user's file to another. Private buckets stay unsigned-public.

supporting.justification: Payments in India, including UPI, should go through an RBI-authorised payment aggregator. Razorpay is that aggregator. Card numbers and UPI secrets stay on their side, which keeps this app out of full PCI scope.

alternatives.why_not: Cashfree is the other large India aggregator. Razorpay was chosen for payouts and the docs a small team will actually read.

tradeoffs: Do not store PAN, CVV, or UPI PIN. If you do, PCI scope explodes and this recommendation no longer holds.

supporting.justification: inference is a separate scale problem from the API. A managed endpoint in the same region keeps training data and request payloads next to the ledger or the product database.

alternatives.why_not: It is the right fallback if the managed endpoint's minimum bill is hard to justify. It puts model ops back on the team.

tradeoffs: A real-time endpoint has a floor cost even at night. Serverless inference is cheaper if the model is small and the latency budget allows a cold start.

supporting.justification: A short pipeline: test, then deploy with short-lived cloud credentials. Keep production secrets out of the repo.

alternatives.why_not: It is a fine CI. It is also a second account this team has not said they already run.

tradeoffs: A green pipeline is not a test plan. Someone still has to write the tests.

supporting.justification: Availability target is 99.95. You need a health check, a latency chart, and an alert that reaches a person. Keep the logs in the same region as the data.

alternatives.why_not: More moving parts, or a log vendor that may store text outside the pin.

tradeoffs: Log volume is a bill. Sample debug lines. Do not log OTP codes, tokens, or payment payloads.

assumptions: Compute (aws_ecs, large band) about 300 to 900 USD.
PostgreSQL (aws, large band) about 500 to 1600 USD. High availability doubles the database line.
Object storage is priced near 0.023 USD per GB-month plus requests. Egress is the part that moves the top of the band.
CloudFront for public web assets only. Private objects stay off the CDN.
Payment gateway fees are a percentage of volume and are not in this infra band.
SMS OTP is usage priced. The band assumes a fraction of users request a code each month, about 0.004 USD per active user, and ignores promotional SMS.
Model inference (large band) about 200 to 700 USD, before you retrain.
CloudWatch logs and metrics. The top of the band is chatty debug logs.
CI minutes are assumed inside the free tier for this team size.
SQS at this volume is close to free.
Scale band is large: 300000 users at 12 months, peak 10000, 500.0 GB stored.
This is an order-of-magnitude band, not an invoice. Taxes, support plans, and human time are excluded.

warnings.message: The target is 99.95 and operations.on_call is false. The computers cannot page themselves. Name a human or lower the target.
RBI wants the full payment record stored only in India. Backups, replicas, and log archives stay in India too (for AWS, ap-south-1 and ap-south-2). Do not add a Singapore standby.
OTP SMS is usage priced and can pass the infra budget on its own. Cap retries, and watch the SMS bill as a separate line.
The MVP window is 16 weeks. A hybrid across android, ios, web usually wants about 18 weeks for a team this size. Cut scope before you cut the hard constraints.
DPDP applies. You still need a lawful purpose, a consent or legitimate-use record, a retention period, and a way for a person to access or erase their data. The region pin is not the whole duty.
Keep card data at the payment aggregator and this app stays on the short PCI questionnaire. The moment you store PAN or CVV, stop and redesign.
ISO 27001 or SOC 2 on the vendor does not certify this product. You still need access reviews, backups, and an owner for incidents.

assumptions: budget.existing_licences defaulted to an empty list.
scale.geographic_spread defaulted to national because data_residency is india.
data.sensitivity defaulted to restricted because a strict compliance regime is set.
requirements.expected_rps_peak was not set. Capacity uses peak concurrency (10000), which is roughly 1000 requests per second if about one in ten connected users acts at once.
